clinical_knowledge.topic: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: painless neck lumps, drenching night sweats, and 15-pound weight loss over 3 months

Key HPI features: 24F presents with 3-month history of painless, rubbery swelling on the right side of her neck and above her collarbone. Reports drenching night sweats requiring her to change pajamas every night, unexplained low-grade fevers, and 15-pound weight loss. Also notes severe itching after drinking wine.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 37.9C, HR 88. 3 cm firm, rubbery, nontender right cervical and 2 cm right supraclavicular lymph nodes palpable. No splenomegaly. Bloods: FBC shows mild normocytic anemia, ESR 68 mm/hr, LDH elevated at 340 U/L. Excisional lymph node biopsy reveals Reed-Sternberg cells (binucleated 'owl-eye' appearance, CD15+, CD30+) within a collagen-banded background.
Relevant background/PMH: Treated for presumed lymphadenitis by GP with amoxicillin 1 month ago without effect
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Non-Hodgkin lymphoma without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) — signal more advanced disease.
management_principles: Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy)
Refer to medical oncology for initiation of ABVD chemotherapy regimen (Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine)
Offer fertility preservation counseling prior to treatment
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 24F presenting with classic 'B symptoms' (night sweats, fever, weight loss), alcohol-induced pruritus, and painless cervical/supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 37.9C, HR 88. 3 cm firm, rubbery, nontender right cervical and 2 cm right supraclavicular lymph nodes palpable. No splenomegaly. Bloods: FBC shows mild normocytic anemia, ESR 68 mm/hr, LDH elevated at 340 U/L. Excisional lymph node biopsy reveals Reed-Sternberg cells (binucleated 'owl-eye' appearance, CD15+, CD30+) within a collagen-banded background.
reference_soap.assessment: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype, clinical stage IIB (pending PET-CT).
reference_soap.plan: Order staging baseline PET-CT scan from neck to pelvis and echocardiogram/PFTs (before chemotherapy). Refer to medical oncology for initiation of ABVD chemotherapy regimen (Doxorubicin, Bleomycin, Vinblastine, Dacarbazine). Offer fertility preservation counseling prior to treatment.

learning_objectives: Correlate classic 'B symptoms' and painless lymphadenopathy with Hodgkin/Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
Identify Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+, CD30+) on excisional lymph node biopsy
Outline systematic staging protocol including PET-CT and baseline cardiopulmonary toxicity screens
Counsel young adult oncology patients on oncofertility preservation options prior to chemotherapy

teaching.one_liner: A lymph node cancer marked by painless, rubbery lymphadenopathy, drenching night sweats, weight loss, and — classically — itching triggered by alcohol.
red_flags: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) — signal more advanced disease

must_ask.say: Is the lump painless and rubbery, and has it been growing?
Have you had night sweats heavy enough to soak your clothes, fevers, or weight loss?
Does the area itch or hurt after drinking alcohol?
How many months has the lump been there?
Did antibiotics from your doctor make any difference?

history.answer: I have had these painless lumps on the right side of my neck and above my collarbone for three months, and lately I've been waking up drenched in sweat.
I first felt a small bump on the right side of my neck about three months ago, and over the past month it has grown noticeably larger along with another lump just above my collarbone.
They are both on the right side—one along the side of my neck and another smaller one just above my right collarbone.
They feel firm and somewhat rubbery, like a hard eraser, and they do not seem attached to the skin.
There are two distinct lumps on my neck, and I have checked my armpits and groin but have not felt any lumps anywhere else.
No, they do not hurt at all, even when I press right on them.
No, they stay in the exact same spot when I swallow water or stick my tongue out.
No, they do not change in size or become painful while I am eating.
No, I haven't had a sore throat, cold symptoms, mouth ulcers, or any dental problems recently.
Yes, I have been having unexplained low-grade fevers and drenching night sweats every night that force me to change my pajamas.
Yes, I have lost about 15 pounds over the last three months without trying to diet or exercise more.
Actually, yes—whenever I have a glass of wine, my whole body and neck start itching intensely shortly afterward.
My general doctor prescribed a course of amoxicillin about a month ago for presumed infection, but it did not shrink the lumps at all.
No, I have not had any trouble swallowing, hoarseness in my voice, or shortness of breath.
No, I haven't had any earaches, blocked nose, nosebleeds, or pain when I swallow.
No, I haven't noticed any heart racing, heat or cold intolerance, or trembling in my hands.
No, I have never had tuberculosis, and as far as I know, I have never been exposed to anyone with it.
No, I don't own any pets and haven't handled cats or been scratched by animals.
No, I never received any radiation treatments to my head or neck as a child.
I was wondering if it might be swollen glands from lingering mono or just extreme stress from graduate school.
I am really frightened because the lumps keep getting bigger despite taking that round of antibiotics.
I would really like to get a definitive biopsy done to find out what these lumps are and why I keep sweating so much at night.
I have generally been healthy with no chronic medical conditions, other than this swelling over the last three months.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital before.
I only take a daily oral contraceptive pill, and I took that amoxicillin course a month ago.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or vaping products.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine socially, but I've stopped recently because it triggers that awful itching.
I am a graduate student living in an apartment off campus with a roommate.
No one in my family has had thyroid cancer, leukemia, or any other cancers that I know of.
My last menstrual period started about two weeks ago, and my cycles are very regular on the birth control pill.
I take the birth control pill every day and use condoms, so there is no chance that I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Temperature 37.9°C, blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Young woman sitting comfortably, appearing mildly fatigued with visible fullness on the right lower neck, in no acute distress.
Mild conjunctival pallor present bilaterally; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Oral mucosa is pink and moist, tonsils are symmetric and not enlarged, and posterior pharynx is without erythema or exudate.
A 3 cm firm, rubbery, non-tender right cervical node and a 2 cm firm, non-tender right supraclavicular node are palpable; neither moves with swallowing.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and rises normally with swallowing without discrete nodules or bruits.
No palpable axillary lymphadenopathy bilaterally, and no breast masses are identified.
No palpable inguinal lymphadenopathy bilaterally, and no inguinal hernias are identified.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds and no wheezes or crackles.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs heard.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without palpable masses or guarding.
Liver edge is smooth and non-tender at the costal margin; spleen is not palpable and no splenomegaly is detected.
Skin is warm without jaundice, active rash, petechiae, or obvious excoriations.
